newsitem.title: UK: BOE warns mortgage lenders on aggressive expansion.
newsitem.headline: BOE warns mortgage lenders on aggressive expansion.

text.p: The current level of competition in the UK mortgage market is not giving cause for concern but any aggressive move beyond safe retail-funded lending could be dangerous, the Bank of England said on Monday.

In an article in its latest Financial Stability Review, the Bank says, "Our analysis of various worst-case scenarios makes it clear that the current levels of competition for mortgage business do not represent a general prudential concern."
It says lenders are well capitalised, enjoy a substantial endowment of non-interest bearing liabilities and are mostly retail-funded.
But any move beyond this form of funding in order to pursue wholesale financed expansion would be a concern, the Bank adds.
The Bank also sees the possibility that major lenders will see their benign retail franchise eroded in years to come by increased competition and new technology.
"Such developments might well usher in a harsher world for mortgage lenders, eroding their earnings and limiting their ability to manage their spreads," the study says.
These changes will increase risk and test lenders' risk management capabilities, the Bank concludes.
The Bank comes to the conclusion that despite intense competition, mortgage margins are only slightly narrower than in the 1980s.
Methods such as cashbacks and interest rate discounts have not been enough to change the fact that mortgage lending remains, in the Bank's words, "a safe and profitable business."

Britain's largest mortgage lender is the soon to be floated Halifax Building Society, which has a market share of around 20 percent, followed Abbey National with 12 percent and Lloyds TSB with nearly 10 percent.
